Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the chase.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

India will be very pleased with how they performed, Renuka Singh took three and was the pick. Radha Yadav was also brilliant. The former started things brilliantly and the latter ended it in fine fashion. Overall though, almost all the bowlers played thier part and have put India in a strong position. They now would back themselves to chase this down. Bangladesh on the other hand, need a miracle to defend this. Stay tuned for the second half.

That decision of batting first seems to have backfired big time! The total Bangladesh has got is nowhere close to what they would have thought could challenge this strong Indian team. At one stage though, their position was even worse when they lost 6 wickets for less than 50. Shorna Akter and Nigar Sultana though put up a decent stand and took them to the 80-run mark. They could have got closer to the 90-run mark but they failed to score any run in the last over.
A maiden, the last over of the innings is a double wicket maiden! Fuller and on off, Marufa Akter jams it back to the bowler. Bangladesh Women have ended with 80!

OUT! Renuka Singh sticks to her plan and gets the first wicket of this game. Inswinging delivery on the pads, just that the length was dragged back a fraction on this occasion. Dilara Akter looks to take on Uma Chetry at deep mid-wicket region but miscues it off the cue end and straight in the safe hands of Uma Chetry at the fence.
Commentary.Howout: c Uma Chetry b Renuka Singh

SIX! Dilara Akter starts scoring with a biggie. Fuller, on pads. Dilara Akter flicks this with the breeze and that helps the ball sail over the fence and into the stands towards deep square leg region.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Inswinging, fuller one on leg. Dilara Akter stays inside her crease and looks to flick but misses. Richa Ghosh comes up to the stumps to negate the batters walking down the track. Wide signaled.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Renuka Singh to Dilara Akter, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Starts with an inswinging delivery on off, Dilara Akter looks to tuck this around on leg. Gets an inside edge onto her pads and back to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Renuka Singh to Dilara Akter, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all in readiness now. The two umpires have made their way to the middle followed by the players of India Women who scatter to their respective field positions. Dilara Akter and Murshida Khatun are going to be the openers for Bangladesh Women. Renuka Singh, on the other hand, will open the attack with the ball for India Women.
Time for pre-match formalities as the teams walk out for their respective National Anthems. It is going to be the National Anthem of India first followed by that of Bangladesh.
Marina Iqbal says that it is a good surface and there is a bit of grass cover. Adds that the batters will try and dominate the shorter boundary but the spinners might find some assistance as well.

The skipper of India Women, Harmanpreet Kaur says they have played good cricket so far and will be looking to back themselves today as well. Adds that the important thing is to play well and toss doesn't hold a lot of importance. Mentions that the Bangladesh Women's side is competitive and they always make life difficult.

The skipper of Bangladesh Women, Nigar Sultana says that the wicket looks good hence they want to bat freely. Adds that it is about partnerships and they need to work on their batting unit. Mentions that Sabinkun Jesmin is out.
Bangladesh Women (Playing XI) - Dilara Akter (WK), Murshida Khatun, Nigar Sultana (C), Rumana Ahmed, Ishma Tanjim, Ritu Moni, Rabeya Khan, Shorna Akter, Nahida Akter, Jahanara Alam, Marufa Akter.

India Women (Playing XI) - Shafali Verma, Smriti Mandhana, Uma Chetry, Harmanpreet Kaur (C), Jemimah Rodrigues, Richa Ghosh (WK), Deepti Sharma, Pooja Vastrakar, Radha Yadav, Tanuja Kanwar, Renuka Singh.
TOSS - The coin is flipped and it lands in favor of Bangladesh Women, their skipper Nigar Sultana opts to BAT first.

Bangladesh Women, on the other hand, started their campaign with a defeat against Sri Lanka Women but they bounced back and won the remaining contests comprehensively. Their last group game was against Malaysia Women and they just ran riots over them. The batting unit clicked in unison and posted a mammoth total against the Malaysian side which they failed to chase and lost by a hefty margin of 114 runs. The joyful sight for the skipper and team management was the top order scoring the bulk of runs. Murshida Khatun and Dilara Akter form a good pair right at the top and Nigar Sultana, Rumana Ahmed, and Ritu Moni combine to provide a solid base in the middle order. The bowling has done well too with Nahida Akter, Rabeya Khan, Jahanara Alam and Shorna Akter picking up wickets regularly throughout the tournament. Cricket is a game of uncertainties, and even the strongest teams can have off days. On the other hand, underdog teams can rise to the occasion and cause upsets. As the great cricket saying goes, "Any team can beat any team on their day." Can Bangladesh Women pull off an upset against India Women? We shall find out soon. Stay tuned for toss and team updates...

India Women won three out of three in the group stage. The side never got into a contest against any of their opponents so far. India Women have ticked all the boxes entering into the knockout stage with their batting firing on all cylinders while the bowling complementing them perfectly. The side has fielded well too. Skipper Harmanpreet Kaur rested herself in their last league stage game and it was Smriti Mandhana who led the side in her absence. Dayalan Hemalatha, after being promoted to open the innings spent some valuable time in the middle with the bat. Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana continue to showcase their skillset and prove deadly right at the top while Harmanpreet Kaur, Jemimah Rodrigues, and Richa Ghosh carry the momentum given by the top order. Renuka Singh and Arundhati Reddy have formed a good bowling pair at the top with the spin of Deepti Sharma and Radha Yadav to complement them perfectly. India Women have stood firm to their tag of being the favorites to win this tournament.

Hello and welcome folks. It is showtime in the ACC Women's Asia Cup T20 as we are down to the last four. The first semi-final will be played between the Group A winners, India Women vs the Group B runner's up, Bangladesh Women. The game will be played at Rangiri Dambulla International Stadium, Dambulla.
... MATCHDAY ...

A week after the start of Asia's premier women's cricket tournament, the ACC Women's T20 Asia Cup 2024, we now have the top four teams who are set to compete for a coveted spot in the grand finale. The first semi-final will feature a showdown between this season's undefeated and reigning champions, India Women, and the resilient Bangladesh Women. This exciting clash will take place at the Rangiri Dambulla International Stadium in Dambulla, promising to be another epic battle for the history books. India Women have demonstrated remarkable consistency throughout the tournament, performing cohesively as a unit, making them a formidable force and clear favourites to retain the title. Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma have been prolific run-scorers, setting the tone with their explosive batting at the top of the order. Harmanpreet Kaur, in her couple of appearances, has been solid, and alongside Jemimah Rodrigues and Richa Ghosh, has strengthened the batting lineup, making it formidable. The pace unit led by Renuka Singh has delivered crucial early breakthroughs, which have been effectively capitalized on by the spin duo of Deepti Sharma and Radha Yadav. The team looks like a well-oiled machine and will be poised for success as they head into the knockout stage. Bangladesh Women, after losing their first game, made a strong comeback by winning the next two matches comprehensively, securing their place in the semi-finals. Murshida Khatun has led the batting unit effectively, and skipper Nigar Sultana has had a couple of notable performances where she remained unbeaten. Apart from the initial setback against Sri Lanka Women, the batting lineup has shown considerable strength. They will face a significant challenge in maintaining this momentum against the formidable India Women bowlers. Nahida Akter and Rubya Haider have been among the key wicket-takers and will need additional support from the rest of the bowling attack to make a significant impact. With a history of close and intense matches between these two teams, this semi-final clash promises to be an edge-of-the-seat thriller. Who will prevail and secure a spot in the grand finale? We'll find out soon!
